entries.title: A decorrelating stationary Gaussian sequence crosses every fixed threshold infinitely often
entries.statement: Let (X_n)_{n>=1} be a stationary centered real Gaussian sequence with variance sigma^2 in (0,infinity) and Cov(X_1,X_{1+h}) tending to zero as h tends to infinity. For every finite rho>0, P(rho+X_n<0 for infinitely many n)=1. The one-point negative probability is Phi(-rho/sigma)>0. No independence of the full sequence is assumed.
entries.proof_text: Put I_n=1_{X_n<-rho} and p=E I_n=Phi(-rho/sigma)>0. The joint normal law of (X_1,X_{1+h}) tends to two independent normals as its correlation tends to zero; because the threshold boundary has zero Gaussian mass, c_h=Cov(I_1,I_{1+h}) tends to zero. For A_N=N^{-1} sum_{n=1}^N I_n, stationarity gives Var(A_N)=p(1-p)/N+2 N^{-2} sum_{h=1}^{N-1}(N-h)c_h, which tends to zero by splitting at a fixed H and then sending H to infinity. If every I_n on a fixed tail were zero, the corresponding average would be zero; Chebyshev bounds that event by Var(A_N)/p^2 and makes its probability zero. The countable union over starting tails is the event of finitely many crossings, hence also has probability zero.
assumptions: Joint Gaussianity, stationarity, and zero mean
Variance sigma^2 is finite and strictly positive

entries.title: An additive Gaussian elastic density cannot equal a nonnegative smoothed particle density
entries.statement: Fix beta,a,b,Lambda,rho>0 and 0<s<2. In the stipulated planar Gaussian displacement-increment model with Fourier covariance beta^{-1}1_{0<|k|<=Lambda}[P_L(k)/(a|k|^s)+P_T(k)/(b|k|^2)] and inverse Fourier measure d^2k/(2pi)^2, let delta rho=-rho div u. Then Var(delta rho(0))=rho^2 Lambda^{4-s}/[2pi beta a(4-s)]>0; rho+delta rho is negative infinitely often on any fixed equally spaced ray almost surely. Therefore it cannot have the exact one-point law of a finite smoothing sum of any locally finite point configuration with a nonnegative kernel. This concerns only the auxiliary Gaussian model, not an actual Riesz Gibbs law or a controlled approximation.
entries.proof_text: The divergence multiplier annihilates P_T and contracts P_L to |k|^2, so the density spectral function is f(k)=rho^2 |k|^{2-s}1_{|k|<=Lambda}/(beta a). Integrating in polar coordinates yields the stated positive variance. Since f is integrable, its covariance tends to zero by the Riemann-Lebesgue lemma. Values along an equally spaced ray form a stationary nondegenerate Gaussian sequence, so the preceding threshold-crossing lemma applies. A finite smoothing sum of nonnegative kernel values is pointwise nonnegative, whereas this additive Gaussian has a strictly positive negative one-point tail.
assumptions: Gaussian covariance is stipulated, not derived from Riesz particles
The comparison particle smoothing kernel is nonnegative and its sum is finite
Equality means exact equality of one-point laws, not an approximation

relations.rationale: The almost-sure negative-density conclusion applies the stationary-Gaussian threshold lemma after verifying covariance decay.
This reviewed auxiliary obstruction concerns a proposed exact density identification used in approaches to P0321; it neither proves nor refutes the open-problem card.
